references.citation: Emotional Dependency: A Threat to Close Friendships (InterVarsity Press, 1990; first published by Love in Action, 1984, and by Exodus International–North America, 1987). National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428, Box 2, Folder 9.
references.about: A booklet on close friendships between women that called such a friendship between women "emotional dependency" and a sin, listed its warning signs, and told readers how to end it; the tape quotes its definition, its signs, its marriage exception and its warning of grief.

references.citation: Exodus Global Alliance, "Women" resources page ("Emotional Dependency, 5 Pack … Package of 5"), Internet Archive capture of 11 June 2016: web.archive.org/web/20160611170337/http://www.exodusglobalalliance.org/forwomenp521.php, read 15 Nov 2026.
references.about: A ministry network's online shop that still sold the 1987 booklet in packs of five for women's groups in June 2016; the tape's trailer sells it the same way.

references.short: The Heart of the Matter, Focus on the Family, 2001
references.citation: Focus on the Family, The Heart of the Matter: The Roots and Causes of Female Homosexuality (© 2001). National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428, Box 6, Folder 4.
references.pages: printed p. 10 (PDF p. 8): "three primary conditions"; printed p. 14 (PDF p. 10): "an identity crisis"
references.about: A booklet that taught that lesbianism grows from "three primary conditions" in a woman's past and is "not a sexual orientation problem" but "an identity crisis"; the tape's first chapter fills in its words.

references.citation: Exodus International–North America, Are People Born Gay? Understanding the Roots of Homosexuality, booklet #PR-02 (© 1993). National Museum of American History, Archives Center, NMAH.AC.1428, Box 2, Folder 12.
references.pages: printed p. 19 (PDF p. 11), read on the page image
references.about: A booklet that explained a lesbian woman with a computer analogy: a heterosexual woman has a floppy disc titled "woman", a lesbian woman "has no file to put it in"; the tape's third chapter reads it word for word.

notes.heading: What the bar no longer carries (v5 showed these in its margin; the bar now carries only the source of what is said)

items.text: The World Health Organization's office for the Americas said in May 2012 that homosexuality is not an illness, "and therefore it requires no cure", and that "cures" lack medical justification.
items.source: Pan American Health Organization (Regional Office of the WHO for the Americas), "'Cures' for an illness that does not exist", position statement, May 2012, p. 1; news release 17 May 2012, paho.org/en/news/17-5-2012-therapies-change-sexual-orientation-lack-medical-justification-and-threaten-health, read 15 Nov 2026.

items.text: The Royal College of Psychiatrists said in April 2014: "There is no sound scientific evidence that sexual orientation can be changed."
items.source: Royal College of Psychiatrists, Position Statement PS02/2014 (April 2014), p. 2, https://www.rcpsych.ac.uk/docs/default-source/improving-care/better-mh-policy/position-statements/ps02_2014.pdf?sfvrsn=b39bd77c_4

items.text: Exodus International, which published booklets [1] and [4], announced on 19 June 2013, at its own conference, that it was closing; its president apologised.
items.source: Religion News Service in The Christian Century (24 July 2013 issue), "'Ex-gay' group closes as its president apologizes", christiancentury.org/article/2013-06/ex-gay-group-exodus-international-shuts-down-president-apologizes, read 15 Nov 2026.

notes.heading: Real and invented on this tape

items.text: Heartwood, Heartwood Ministries, the DVD menu, the Viewer Guide pages and the chapter titles are invented. The form is real: small-group DVD courses with a Leader's Edition and a discussion guide were sold to churches in the 2010s.
items.source: Restored Hope Network, "Suggested Books by Category" (PDF, August 2014), p. 1 (Such Were Some of You, a DVD "video curriculum", Regular and Leader's Edition); review at dove.org/review/10417-such-were-some-of-you/, read 15 Nov 2026.

items.text: The trailer "Too Close?" is invented copy. What it sells is real: the booklet [1] with its checklist of signs (printed pp. 8–9, 15), sold for $1 and, in June 2016, in packs of five [2].
items.source: Emotional Dependency, 1987 edition (Exodus International–North America), NMAH.AC.1428 Box 2 Folder 9, PDF p. 15 (the $1 price); Focus on the Family order page, "With a checklist", $1 (The Heart of the Matter, PDF p. 21); [2].

items.text: The lesson's end credits ("© 2016 Heartwood Ministries. Every copy you buy plants another seed.") are invented, in a ministry's voice. In v5 they opened the disc; he asked for them at the end of the lesson.
items.source: invented (the piece); his note on v5, 15 Nov 2026

items.text: Spoken lines that the documents do not give word for word are the course's own framing: "Grab your journal and your workbook, friend. Today we go underneath.", "Here's a picture from an older teaching… Remember floppy disks?", "Save that one, friend.", and the trailer's copy. The teaching in between is quoted or closely paraphrased, with its page in the bar.

notes.heading: Moved off the tape (v5 had them; the two-minute tape does not)

items.text: The "Deep Roots" trailer: a church's Living Waters group, March 2016: "Monday evenings at 7 p.m. for 20 weeks"; "The cost is $150 (payment plans are available)"; "Groups fill up in a matter of days".
items.source: A church counselling centre's "Living Waters" group page, posted 29 March 2016, a public page read 15 Nov 2026 (its address carries a person's name, so it is not printed here).

items.text: The chapter on mothers and fathers: "defensive detachment" (a girl who pulls back from a mother "perceived as distant, bitter, critical, overbearing and unloving") and the father's "score card of passing or failing as a little girl".
items.source: The Heart of the Matter [3], printed p. 17 (PDF p. 11); Are People Born Gay? [4], printed p. 8 (PDF p. 6).
